README: Sound follows the recurring lie-block clank, then lets the honest confession clear it. Cues and spoken words anchor every event; run scripts/sound.py build after edits.

sections.why: Cold open: the lantern is in danger before the story rewinds.
Daylight reveals the impossible rule and the friends' bright lantern plan.
The blue ribbon is a wish, and the friend plants the promise to fix things together.
The switch breaks, and the teller starts hiding what he did.
The storm and the accumulated weight push the teller to the edge.
The first honest confession changes the danger into a chance to help each other.

beds.why: The cold-open gust around the parade lantern.
Open schoolyard air while the friends build and plan.
The parade route at night, under every lie and the final repair.
Rain and wind rise with the lantern's near-fall.
The waiting parade crowd cheers once the lantern lights again.

sfx.why: The first Netherite block enters the pack.
A storm gust blows through the opening picture.
His knees hit the ground under the first block.
The cold open cuts back to the bright daytime build.
The friends set their lantern frame onto the parade cart.
Cloth shifts as the two friends lift the frame together.
The finished lantern is their bright parade hope.
A single cube demonstrates the rule of the power.
Only the teller notices the impossible cube.
Truth makes the demonstration block disappear (trimmed 5 dB: at full level it left the voice only 4 dB above the mix; at 7 it fell under the music).
The blank block gives him no hint about what to confess.
A brief pulse under the warning about the real danger.
The stakes fall dark on 'pass away'.
He tries to sound certain about a switch he never tested.
The first lie in the story adds its matching block.
He tells the truth and clears that first block.
The next beat turns from the rule to the blue-ribbon wish.
The little blue ribbon marks the prize they hope to win.
The friend's promise to fix the lantern together.
The story turns to the night parade and its new mistake.
The teller breaks the redstone switch while showing off.
His denial is immediately false.
The denial adds one cube to the pack.
He turns away and tries to hide the strain.
Cut to the friend offering a chance to repair the lantern.
The friend asks if he can fix it.
The 'by myself' lie adds another Netherite block.
He searches an empty pocket for a switch that is not there.
The false spare-switch claim adds a third block.
The growing stack drags him down onto his knees (trimmed -5 dB: measured, it left the voice only 3-5 dB above the mix, the tightest moment in the film).
The next shot isolates the lantern's red fault light.
The switch is still broken, not warming up.
Another lie adds the fourth cube.
His feet drag as the added weight slows him.
Cut to the friend noticing the teller's sweat and strain.
A small warning as the friend spots the sweat.
His friend asks if he is okay; a quiet pulse becomes audible under the question.
The fifth lie adds the heaviest cube yet.
One close, restrained pulse as he struggles to breathe.
The fear tightens as his chest does.
The schoolyard storms over as the climax begins.
A gust drives the rain and yanks the lantern sideways.
Wind rises into the lantern's dangerous swing.
The friend catches and braces the lantern's rope.
Two slow, wet steps toward the friend.
The blocks drag against every attempted step.
The weight wins and drops him onto his knees.
One restrained pulse holds the danger of passing away (trimmed -4 dB: measured, it left the voice only 3-5 dB above the mix, the tightest moment in the film).
The edge of the danger lands on 'away' (trimmed -4 dB: measured, it left the voice only 3-5 dB above the mix, the tightest moment in the film).
Cut into the first honest confession.
Owning the broken switch removes the first matching block.
The reveal: the lie, not the lantern, has been weighing him down.
His second confession clears the block from the invented spare (trimmed -4 dB: measured, it left the voice only 3-5 dB above the mix, the tightest moment in the film).
Two blocks finish fading, leaving three still pinned to him.
The next truth starts with the three blocks that still remain.
The remaining cubes keep his shoulders and knees down.
The friend strains to keep one hand on the rope.
The friend's free hand reaches toward the teller.
He names the warming-switch lie and its block begins to clear.
He admits he was scared, not fine.
The final admission releases the last invisible weight.
The words 'I needed you' turn the confession into a request for help.
The next beat begins as the friend pulls him up.
The friend lifts him as the weight releases.
The friends set the repaired switch back into place.
Together they steady the crooked lantern on its cart.
The lantern glows again after the repair.
The parade crowd responds when the lantern lights.
A final quiet cut to the empty pack beside the lantern.
He sets down the now-empty cloth pack.
The pack settles on the ground beside their lantern.
A warm, small button on the subscribe line, not a new music swell.
